Indonesia Seizes Chinese Chemical Cargo Bound for Bangladesh

Indonesia intercepted a Comoros-flagged cargo ship, MV Star Line, on November 7 in waters off Belawan, North Sumatra. The ship was traveling from Lianyungang Port in China to Mongla Port in Bangladesh. Indonesian authorities seized a cargo identified as sodium perchlorate, a chemical used in missile production. One report suggested the cargo could be for 100 missiles and also included millions of 4G SIM cards. The seizure has raised questions about potential destabilization efforts in India's Northeast, with one report drawing a parallel to a 2004 incident.
